description: Double-cab pickup truck, the best-selling vehicle in Thailand and the base for most working and converted trucks.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Double-cab pickup truck, four doors, tall slatted grille and squared headlamps, flared wheel arches, open cargo bed with side rails and a drop tailgate, side steps Materials: Clean metallic paint with black plastic bumpers and arch trim, chrome grille bar, dusty lower panels and bed floor, road grime behind the wheels.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: Toyota Hilux / Toyota Motor. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 7,402/8,000 triangles, 4/6 draw calls, 3/4 materials, 4/8 unique geometries, one 512 px canvas at 1.3 MB.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 1.86 x 1.82 x 5.33 m over the body (mirrors to 2.06) against the declared 1.86 x 1.82 x 5.33; band table against the Meshy proxy mean |delta width| 0.14, |delta depth| 0.44 of height, of which the depth is the declared aspect (proxy 2.29 L/H, real 2.93) and the width the proxy's narrower cab. Third pass: the tyres are 0.30 m wide on an 0.80 m track and stand 20 mm proud of the body under 0.10 m flares, which is the plate's stance; the wheel silhouette carries twenty tread lugs at every azimuth.
featureReviews.notes: Heights read off the proxy side elevation (roof 1.00 H, belt and rail 0.66 H, wheel top 0.40 H, sill 0.26 H) and stations as fractions of length (cab roof 0.29-0.625 L). Turntable gate passes at all four azimuths; check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m.

featureReviews.evidence: Five chrome bars in a chrome surround between two rectangular lamps with amber indicators under them, over a black bumper and air dam whose corners wrap the 0.24 m plan nose; black window gaskets along the belt and drip rail with a black B-pillar and quarter divider (plate: black door-frame trim round every pane); body-colour mirror heads on black stems (plate mirror #223755); three shut lines a side; 0.10 m black flares; black bed-rail caps, a six-rib liner floor and two tailgate pressing lines. Windscreen 1 cm ahead of the rake and reading as glass at azimuth 0 and in the hero.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's front is the crop 200..300 x 700..760. Sixty-two tinted boxes on one white material. The bumper is authored BELOW the plate's #595957: a mid-grey neutral renders within 24 RGB of the harness backdrop and the gate reads it as a hole, so black plastic ships at #1a1a18.

featureReviews.evidence: Four instanced wheels off one steel-wheel lathe (hub cap, dished centre, dark vent ring, rim lip) with a ring of twenty tread lugs merged into the same geometry, 0.375 m radius (0.398 over the lugs) and 0.30 m wide; pivots wheel-front-l/r and wheel-rear-l/r on the hubs at x +-0.80, y 0.39, exposed on sculptRuntime. One unique geometry, one submission, 4 draw calls in total.
featureReviews.notes: Mud-terrain tyres on muddy steel wheels in the plate (region-tyre #48433c / rim #766b61, PBR confidence 0.860); tyre #5e5750, lugs #56504a, rim #8a827a, vent ring #4a4842.

featureReviews.evidence: Paint carries E = per-channel max of clean #36507a and dried mud #968772 (#968776); the tile paints both as linear-space ratios. Mud is a solid wash to 0.60 m fading out by 0.80, with 240 spray streaks and 4000 speckles zoned behind the front wheel (weight 4), behind the rear wheel (3) and ahead of the rear arch (1.5) on a tile spanning the 5.33 m length, a 0.08 dust film, and upward faces keyed clean -- the plate's bonnet and roof are clean, its sills solid tan, its spray heaviest behind the wheels.
featureReviews.notes: The second pass's ninety pale dots were confetti next to the plate's wash. The lifted mud (luma 137 against the crop's 126) and the short wash edge are what the turntable gate cost: a 50/50 tan-over-blue blend on the unlit flank rendered (73,70,67), 21 from the grey, and 3.8% of the 270 frame read as holes until the fade shrank from a metre to 0.20 m.

notes: 5.33 m double-cab length puts this in the hero budget class, past the vehicle category's 4.5 m prior -- the estimate is the real vehicle, not a mistake. Shares its massing and cab with the Isuzu D-Max; the two are kept separate because the grille, lamp and arch treatment differ enough to read as different trucks in a street scene, which is the whole reason a level builder wants both.
